newsitem.title: USA: Viacom seeks public auction of USA Networks.
newsitem.headline: Viacom seeks public auction of USA Networks.

text.p: Viacom Inc on Monday asked a judge to hold a public auction of USA Networks, the cable partnership jointly owned by Seagram Co Ltd.
According to court documents filed Monday, Viacom chose the auction remedy after its offer to buy Seagram's half of the partnership for $1.94 billion was rejected June 12.

Viacom, which owns Paramount Pictures, MTV and Nickelodeon, and Seagram, which owns entertainment and theme park concern Universal Inc, have been fighting for control of USA Network, with each side accusing the other of violating the terms of the partnership agreement.

In its own filing, Seagram said last month's Delaware Chancery Court finding that Viacom had violated a non-compete provision of the partnership means that Viacom is obliged to sell its share under a buy-sell provision that could prove disadvantageous to New York-based Viacom.

Seagram filed suit against Viacom last year, charging the company with violating the terms of the partnership agreement by launching a new cable channel called "Nick at Nite TV Land." Seagram said the partnership prevents either company from operating or launching entertainment cable networks outside of the USA Network.
However, Viacom contends there is no breach of the partnership, that the partnership is working well and that MCA is trying to get control of USA Network "at an unfairly low price."

The buy-sell provision would allow Seagram either to sell its share to Viacom at the high end of a valuation range or buy Viacom's share at the low end. The range would be the difference between Viacom's estimate of the partnership's worth and the estimate of an independent investment banker.

Seagram also wants Vice Chancellor Myron Steele to order Viacom to dispose of its cable networks or to stop operating them unless, by some unspecified date, Viacom agrees to trigger and abide by the buy-sell provision. According to Seagram, the order would remedy Viacom's breach of the non-compete provision.
Seagram wants Viacom to give back to the partnership any benefits obtained from it since 1994 and to pay Seagram's costs and legal fees.
In a letter rejecting Viacom's $1.94 billion offer to buy, Seagram said "We are not a seller. Universal wishes to remain in the basic cable business through its interest in USA Newtorks."

Viacom maintains that an auction with both sides bidding is the only way to determine "the fair market value of the asset" and alleges that Seagram is only interested in obtaining "ownership of the USA Network joint venture at a price that does not reflect fair market value," court papers say.
Both sides have until July 11 to respond to each other's proposals. Steele will then decide sometime after that his remedy for the dissolution of the partnership agreement.
